chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description:
1. Course Objectives:

The course demonstrates concepts, technology, and applications of advanced event planning.

2. Course Content:

Key topics include: Overview of the event knowledge on planning, operations, marketing, finance, legal aspects, and specialized event types, incorporating practical skills. Additionally, it includes a new module on the application of Artificial Intelligence in event management, equipping students with cutting-edge technological insights to enhance event design, logistics, and marketing.

3. Activities and Teaching Methodology:

Lectures, hands-on sessions, and individual and group projects will help students practice and develop the knowledge and management skill about event industry.

taiLieu: Charles Bladen, James Kennell, Emma Abson, Nick Wilde
clo: Identify the key characteristics of events, events industry bodies, in order to understand the business of events management as a service activity
Understand the scope and scale of the events business and the determinants of demand for events
Identify the social, economic, political impact and developmental implications of running events
Understand the planning process for events, including the budgetary organization of events, marketing, catering and technical provisions.
Identify issues of risk management in terms of event planning, operations and the issues involved in closing down an event
Intergrate a theoratical framework in to an event project
